title: Azriel Chaikin (Chabadpedia, Hebrew)
description: Born 5691 to Rabbi Meir Chaim Chaikin. Married in winter 5716 (1955-56) the daughter of Rabbi Michael Lipsker, shliach in Meknes; the shadchan was Rabbi Binyomin Gorodetsky. The couple settled in Agadir and opened the Beis Rivka girls' school there. Later Denmark (founded Yeshivas Oholei Yosef Yitzchak, Copenhagen; chief rabbi there about ten years). Three children.

title: Michael Lipsker (Chabadpedia, English)
description: Born Poltava 1907 to Rabbi Chaim Tzvi Lipsker and Mrs. Bas Sheva; married Teibel, daughter of the chossid Rabbi Eliyahu Par; Leningrad (siege burials with brother-in-law Rabbi Baruch Shifrin); escaped Russia 1946, Paris; shliach to Morocco from 20 Shvat 1950 (Meknes); later kitchen manager at 770; died 5 Iyar 5745 (1985), age 78, buried Montefiore Cemetery, Queens. Family: son-in-law Rav Azriel Chaikin; brothers Rav Yaakov Lipskar and Rav Aryeh Zev Lipskar.

title: Michael Lipsker (Chabadpedia, Hebrew)

title: Meir Chaim Chaikin (Chabadpedia, Hebrew)
description: Rabbi Meir Chaim Chaikin (5667 - 15 Kislev 5726), son of Rabbi Azriel Chaikin. Studied at Tomchei Temimim in Nevel; rabbi of Surazh (Vitebsk province), then Tiflis; exiled by the Soviets, and in exile married Sarah Chana, daughter of the chossid Eliyahu Shmuel Kahanov. After WWII rabbi of Adas Yisrael, Stockholm; from 5711 in Montreal as rabbi and rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Temimim. Buried at Montefiore Cemetery near the Previous Rebbe's Ohel. Children: Rabbi Azriel, Rabbi Sholom Dovber; sons-in-law R' Nosson Gurary (Montreal) and R' Baruch Bentzion Brikman (Crown Heights).

title: Eliyahu Par (Chabadpedia, Hebrew)
description: Rabbi Eliyahu Kalman Par ('R' Eli'), born c. 5640 (~1880) to Rabbi Moshe; raised funds for Tomchei Temimim in the USSR and was jailed in Vitebsk; later Tel Aviv and Kfar Chabad; died 28 Kislev 5723 (4th night of Chanukah). Daughters: Sonia, wife of Rabbi Baruch Shifrin; Teibel, wife of Rabbi Michael Lipsker.

title: Sholom Dovber Chaikin (Chabadpedia, Hebrew)
description: Born 27 Tammuz 5707 (1947) in Montreal, youngest child of Rabbi Meir Chaim Chaikin and Mrs. Sarah Chana; his great-grandfather was Rabbi Asher Margolis of Rakshik. Married Sheindel-Sheina, daughter of Rabbi Chaim Shneur Zalman Schorr; shliach in London about ten years, then rav of the Chabad community in Cleveland, Ohio; member of Vaad Rabbonei Lubavitch. Children listed are shluchim in Toronto, Montreal, Barbados, Baltimore, Moscow, Philadelphia and elsewhere.

title: Azriel Chaikin (Hebrew Wikipedia)
description: Born 10 Sivan 5690 (June 6, 1930) in the USSR to Rabbi Meir Chaim Chaikin (Gulag prisoner; after 1946 rabbi in Stockholm, later av beis din in Montreal). Left Russia via Poland in 1946 to Paris; 1947 to New York, Tomchei Temimim 770; 1954 rabbi of a Pittsburgh synagogue; 1955 dayan in Montreal; later chief rabbi of Copenhagen and of Belgium; Chief Rabbi of Ukraine Sept 2003 - May 2008. Lives in Crown Heights; three children. Brother: Rabbi Sholom Dovber Chaikin, rav in Cleveland.

Cyla card records birth September 20, 1918 in Pinsk (Arolsen card September 27); both boys’ cards give birthplaces "Kutajsk-USSR" and the same birthdays recorded at Pocking. The cards document a Paris case with a planned Swedish destination, not proof of departure or marital status.

title: Here’s My Story: Nothing to Fear
description: First-person Koppel Bacher interview in October 2010, published 2016. He says he went to 770 in 1955 at fourteen, Montreal two years later, returned South Africa in 1961, marriage advice in 1962, married and came to Rebbe audience, and remembers teaching, family visits and robbery amid unrest. Teacher Greenglass quote is a paraphrase by Koppel, not a verbatim Rebbe transcript.

title: Lipskars celebrate 50 years of following their calling
description: Interviews with Mendel and Mashi Lipskar and Koppel Bacher. Says he financed and brought the Lipskars in 1972, and that he brought other rabbis including Yossy Goldman. It describes a nine-year stay abroad after 1955, in tension with Koppel’s first-person 1961 return. Its 20 centers and 60-plus shluchim count is as of 2022.

title: The Trailblazers
description: South African communal history says Koppel studied abroad from fourteen in 1955, then chose family wholesaling rather than formal rabbinate, joined Yeshiva College board, late-1960s Kollel Yad Shaul, and helped establish Chabad locally. Its nine-year overseas figure conflicts with Koppel’s first-person 1961 return.
